title: From promise to deployment
subtitle: An October preview of the monthly Atlas. Follow the evidence from expanding services to industrial supply commitments.
coverageNote: A sourced editorial preview covering selected developments. This is not a completed monthly scan of all 50 technologies or two full deep dives. Existing profiles retain their original research dates.

highlights.title: Robotaxis reach more riders
highlights.summary: Waymo reported opening access to everyone in San Antonio, San Diego and Tampa on 14 October. Availability within supported service areas is evidence of expansion; it does not establish city-level profitability.

sources.title: Waymo: October service updates and Toronto plans

highlights.title: Sodium-ion moves toward delivery
highlights.summary: CATL announced a three-year, 60 GWh supply partnership with HyperStrong. The agreement is a commercial milestone, not a count of batteries delivered.

sources.title: CATL and HyperStrong: sodium-ion supply agreement

highlights.title: Compute needs physical infrastructure
highlights.summary: The IEA projects data-centre electricity consumption rising from 485 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030. The 2030 figure is a forecast, not observed demand.

sources.title: IEA: Key Questions on Energy and AI

deepDives.title: Robotaxis: repeatability is the next test
deepDives.summary: Can useful autonomous ride services be reproduced across different cities? This preview separates current access from expansion targets.
findings: Company disclosure: Waymo opened access to everyone in San Antonio, San Diego and Tampa on 14 October, within supported areas.
Company target: its 16 October Toronto announcement aims to welcome first riders in 2028.
Our interpretation: the next assessment should emphasize local service boundaries, weather capability and sustained paid usage.
unknowns: Utilization and reliability across different operating conditions.
deepDives.nextCheck: Look for customer usage, service-area changes and regulatory milestones; keep launch targets separate from delivered service.
deepDives.companyLens: Study the operator, vehicle suppliers and fleet partners as distinct roles. Named relationships require supporting evidence.

sources.title: Waymo: October service updates and Toronto plans

deepDives.title: Sodium-ion: from commitments to installations
deepDives.summary: Which applications can turn manufacturing progress into repeat purchases? Follow shipments and field performance alongside supply announcements.
findings: Company disclosure: CATL and HyperStrong announced a three-year agreement covering 60 GWh of sodium-ion battery supply.
Company target: CATL said Naxtra was set to enter full-scale mass production by the end of 2026.
Our interpretation: installations, reliability and repeat orders will be stronger commercial evidence than commitments alone.
unknowns: Delivered quantities under the HyperStrong agreement.
Independently comparable costs and field performance.
deepDives.nextCheck: Seek customer-confirmed deliveries and operational installations; compare costs only with matching application, scale and measurement conditions.
deepDives.companyLens: Distinguish CATL’s cell manufacturing role from HyperStrong’s integration and deployment role.

sources.title: CATL and HyperStrong: sodium-ion supply agreement

candidates.title: Flexible power for AI
candidates.subtitle: Where computing, storage and grid flexibility meet.
candidates.summary: Proposed research thread: investigate whether flexible data-centre loads and on-site storage can improve grid access and create commercial opportunities. The IEA discusses flexibility as a response to power constraints.
candidates.whyWatch: This connects existing Atlas topics; it has not yet qualified as a separate technology profile.
questions: Which operators have measured flexible-load performance?
Who pays for flexibility, and under what contracts?
candidates.nextCheck: Find distinct customer needs, measured results and a credible company ecosystem before promoting this candidate.
